newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude drifts after resistance test fails.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude drifts after resistance test fails.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were mostly firmer at midday on Thursday, with little action in a quiet, pre-holiday session.
Products were also firmer, following crude, traders said.

At 1330 EDT, July crude was up 10 cents at $21.96 a barrel in lackluster range trading. July unleaded gasoline was up 0.23 cent at 65.10 cents a gallon, while July heating oil was up 0.27 cent at 57.95 cents.

With no news leading sentiment, the session started with an attempt to break July crude through the $22.15 highs of May 19 and May 20. When that failed, stalling at the session high of $22.08, most traders packed it in, floor brokers said.
"We tried to get a little follow-through after yesterday's (firmer) close, but it's become a very boring, pre-holiday market," one broker said.
NYMEX will be closed Monday in observance of the holiday.

"We're going to need some real good news" to break the range, the broker said. He said recent news of hostility between Turkish forces and Iraqi Kurds "dosen't seem to be doing much too the market, but it's giving some underlying support."
